decisions.basis: Names420 constructor requires a nonzero governance timelock through SystemAccess. No current Names420 mutation is governance-only; the dependency is the constructor-bound system authority identity, not ambient ownership or user-name control.
Names420 stores an optional serviceId but does not resolve or authorize through ProtocolRegistry. Security-sensitive consumers that use serviceId must validate Registry state independently.

Names420 has no custody, protocol-admin mutation, or external execution path requiring a local pause dependency. Adding pause authority would broaden control over user naming without a canonical requirement.
Names420 exposes owner/pending-owner lifecycle authorization and no delegated operational capability surface.
Names420 canonical ownership and resolution validity are defined by record state and expiry. No global safety-state gate is specified for these user-authorized state transitions.

Genesis/predeploy initialization remains a deployment requirement handled by deterministic storage generation and manifest binding in NAMES-AUDIT-6; Names420 is not a runtime IGenesisInitializable420 consumer.
Names420 has no proxy/migration entry point. Historical deployment/version migration remains a release/governance concern, not a current runtime dependency.
Names420 accepts direct msg.sender-authorized calls and has no relayed/off-chain signed-command execution path.
Commit/reveal replay protection is local: commitments are committer-bound, age-bounded, consumed on registration, and active leases reject overwrite. Names420 does not consume IReplayProtection420.
Names420 has no signature domain or cross-chain execution requiring on-chain chain-context validation. Wallet/client integrations independently verify chain identity.
Names420 stores label ownership/resolution plus optional profileId/serviceId references; it does not own a mutable metadata document requiring IMetadataCommitment420.

invariants: 420Names runtime authority must not expand merely to satisfy a stale generic dependency list.
Owner and pending-owner checks remain the authority for name lifecycle mutations.
A serviceId stored in a name record does not make the referenced service canonical; consumers validate ProtocolRegistry independently.
Genesis initialization remains mandatory at deployment even though it is not a Names420 runtime interface dependency.
Local commit consumption is the canonical replay defense for registration.

follow_up.NAMES-AUDIT-6: Generate deterministic Genesis state and bind constructor/storage initialization without adding a runtime GenesisInitialization dependency.
follow_up.NAMES-AUDIT-7: Qualify Registry/indexer/search consumption of service references and derived state without promoting those consumers to Names authority.
